title: Ouheywichkingh (Unkechaug village)
summary: Ouheywichkingh is a Dutch-recorded form for an Unkechaug village near Mastic Neck in Brookhaven. The name belongs with the wider Unkechaug place-name record, but it is preserved here because the 1645 treaty form is distinct and historically important.
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern Mastic Neck / Unkechaug-Poospatuck landscape point based on Tooker and Strong; coordinate needs local review.
history_content: Dutch form, Mastic Neck village association, and Unkechaug cross-reference are brought together here. Time-specific diplomatic context is handled as a Timeline Entry with its own reference.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Ouheywichkingh, Ouheywichkinch, and Ouweehacky. The ending is interpreted as a village or place of houses. The whole form is explained as a village or country beyond, matching the Unkechaug sense of land beyond the hill.

Why Place Names Matter

“Recovering Aboriginal place names is also a vital ingredient to revive Aboriginal languages because in daily conversation places are spoken about quite often, and the Aboriginal word can come easily back into use.”

— Jens Korff, Aboriginal place names (2022), 'Reclaiming Aboriginal place names' section
whereintheworld_content: Map location note: near Mastic Neck and the Unkechaug/Poospatuck landscape. The map marker orients readers to the landscape and is not an exact coordinate for the seventeenth-century village or treaty geography.
